chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Wahb ibn Hafsh from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed *dharam* (oath of abstention) from his wife. He said: If he had intercourse with her, then upon him is freeing a slave, or fasting for two consecutive months, or feeding sixty poor people. And if he did not, he is left for three months. If he returned (to intercourse), and if not, he is stopped until he is asked: Do you have a need for your wife, or will you divorce her? If he returned, there is nothing upon him and she is his wife. And if he divorces her (once), he has more right to take her back.

key_terms.رَجْعَةٌ: Revocation of divorce (taking back the wife during the waiting period)
key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: Dharam: An oath of abstention from sexual intercourse

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a husband who swears to abstain from his wife?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* elaborates on the jurisprudence of *Ila'* (oath of abstention), specifying that if the husband resumes relations within the three-month period, he must perform expiation (*kaffarah*) consisting of freeing a slave, fasting for two consecutive months, or feeding sixty poor people. If he persists beyond this period, the wife is given the option to choose between waiting for his decision or initiating a divorce, reflecting the Shia emphasis on protecting the wife's rights during this transitional phase.
